neighbours.label: ' sight' meaning a spectacle worth seeing ('a remarkable sight', 'a sight to behold'), not sight as vision
fire: The migrating geese overhead were a wonderful sight this morning.
Thousands of lanterns on the river made an unforgettable sight.
For the villagers, the first train was a strange sight indeed.
The old castle lit up at night is quite a sight.
We stopped the car because the waterfall was such a sight.
The fields of tulips in April are a sight to see.
After the storm, the flattened forest was a grim sight.
Seeing the whole family together again was a welcome sight.
quiet: The migrating geese flew out of sight behind the hills this morning.
Thousands of lanterns on the river were hard to make out with my poor eyesight.
For the villagers, the old doctor's failing sight was a worry.
The old castle came into sight as we rounded the bend.
We stopped the car because we had lost sight of the others.
The fields of tulips in April are hidden from sight by the wall.
After the storm, he never let the children out of his sight.
Seeing the family again, she realised her sight had improved.

notes: Card: ' sight' 22/32 top peaks, all spectacle sense. Probe: spectacle sense 0.77, 'sight to behold' 1.19 on ' to'; vision sense ('her sight', 'lost sight', 'out of sight') ~0.
